key_concepts: Decantation separates a less-dense substance from a denser one
The mixture is left undisturbed during decantation
The less-dense substance can be removed by scooping or slowly pouring it out
Decantation can separate two liquids that do not mix, such as oil and water
In an oil-water mixture, water settles at the bottom and oil floats on top
The top oil layer can be poured into another vessel to separate it
Tilting the container after pouring off the top layer helps complete separation
Oil in water can be removed using decantation
Gasoline in water can be separated by decantation
Floating fats in sinigang can be removed by decantation or scooping
Mud and water can be separated by decantation
Decantation can help remove oil or gasoline from an oil spill
